title: Buddy Bolden's band, excursions, and Nash's mother's rooming house
summary: Nash knew Bolden when young, describes the small band at picnics and excursions, coin pianos, and says he was about 13.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you have Buddy Bolin in your shop?

Huh? Yeah, I knew him, but I was quite young. See, my mother used to have a rooming house on Howard between Clio and the Rider at 1211 Howard Street. Back at that time, they didn't have no jukebox or nothing like that around in the city. They only had those electric pianos. You'd drop a nickel in them. And then they had those pianos that, it was an anna player, you're pumping with your feet. But whenever a guy come in and could play with his fingers, everybody liked that best. And they had those kind of pianos around here at that time. But the time I'm talking about they had just the old electric piano there. The anna players, they wasn't existing then. The old anna players, you know that you pump with your feet. Those wasn't existing. Just the electric pianos, you drop a nickel in there and the pianos start playing.
What do you remember about Buddy Bolin? Huh?

Buddy Bolin? Well I remember he had a, he played a trumpet. He had a guy who played a violin. He had a guy who played a guitar. He wanted to play the bass and play the drums. They used to play picnic. They used to go all out on these excursions. And so on around there. Excursions used to leave here and go to New Roads, you know. And so on. And at that time, the little, little small band like that used to shine, you know. And all those excursions, you know. And make a lot of money.
Did you go on excursions? No.
That sort of before my time in a way, but I just can't remember, you know. I wasn't fooling on the music around at that time.
Well, I was around about, I would say around 13, going on 14. Around up in there.
